tagline: Along old sand islands, through a town that was not frostproof.
intro: SR 17, called Scenic Highway by the people who live on it, leaves US 27 south of Frostproof and winds 38.7 miles north along the Lake Wales Ridge to Haines City, through Babson Park, Lake Wales, Dundee and Lake Hamilton, past lakes and citrus fields.

The ridge is what is left of a chain of sand islands from two million years ago, when water covered nearly all of Florida, and its white sand still shows in the neighborhoods. Babson Park was Crooked Lake until the economist Roger Babson bought about 400 acres there in 1923 and the town took his name.

moments.title: Frostproof
moments.text: J.W. Carson scratched out Lakemont on the post office application and wrote Frostproof, a promise to would-be landowners that the Great Freeze of 1894 and 1895 broke.

moments.title: Spook Hill
moments.text: On this gravity hill in Lake Wales cars appear to roll uphill, the doing, by one local tale, of a chief and a giant alligator who killed each other here.

moments.title: Bok Tower Gardens
moments.text: Edward Bok had Frederick Law Olmsted Jr. turn a dry sandhill on Iron Mountain into gardens around a 205-foot carillon tower, and flamingos were tried there more than once.

sources.label: Florida Scenic Highways, The Ridge Scenic Highway
